newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids hold steady with crude, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids hold steady with crude, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices, helped by fairly stable crude, held relatively steady Tuesday, but trade remained thin, with buyers relaxed in the typically-weak spring shoulder period, sources said.

"Sooner or later we'll be in the no demand (spring) period, but right now, things feel stable," said one cash trader, noting firm bunkers recently buoyed high sulphur grades, while some interest into Florida helped low sulphur.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at $15.00-25 a barrel, with May one percent paper still straddling $15, traders said.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour also was little changed at $16.00-25 (FOB NYH). A trader said New York Power Authority awarded its tender for 100,000 barrels of HP for April 17-25 delivery at a price within current postings. The trader said the agency was likely to test the fuel oil market with another tender during the first-half of May.
NYH high sulphurs also were flat from Monday, with 2.2 percent still talked in the mid-$14s, traders said.

U.S. Gulf prices were stable, with three percent steady at $13.50 and one percent unchanged at $15.00-25. Traders said a major late Monday sold 45,000 barrels of prompt 2.8 percent (low vanadium, high gravity) at $13.50 (FOB Beaumont, Tx.).

New York city gate gas prices slipped almost a nickel Tuesday to the low-$2.30s/mmBtu, or $14.68 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, held relatively steady at about $2.00/mmBtu, or $12.60 a barrel.
